scope: Primary-source review; zero native tests; no shipping-kernel mapping or exhaustive private-interface claim.

findings.claim: Existing members may continue to fork after a termination request.
The request marks a nonempty coalition; it does not kill its members.
Adoption rejects terminated or reaped state, not merely requested termination.
The management permission check uses privileged-coalition membership.

conclusion: These examined operations alone provide no bounded kill/drain fence. Dedicated-UID fork-fence and privileged-reserve-custody requirements remain open.
